title: The Letter to the Colossians Timeline
sub: The Supremacy of Christ · Against a Local Mix of Philosophy and Legalism
desc: Written to a church Paul had likely never visited, confronting a specific local threat (part philosophy, part legalism, part angel-worship) with one of the highest statements of Christ's identity in the New Testament: the one in whom all things hold together.

eras.label: Era One · Colossians 1
eras.name: The Supremacy of Christ
eras.dates: A church Paul never planted, written to on behalf of a Christ who holds every created thing together

events.title: Greeting and Thanksgiving: A Gospel Bearing Fruit Everywhere
events.detail: Paul, who had likely never visited Colossae in person, thanks God for a faith he heard about secondhand: through Epaphras, the Colossians' own teacher and Paul's fellow servant.

verses.text: “Just as you learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow slave, who is a faithful servant of Christ on our behalf.”

events.title: A Prayer for Full Knowledge and Rescue From Darkness
events.detail: Paul prays for a knowledge that produces action (strength, patience, and thankfulness) grounded in what God has already done: rescuing them from darkness and transferring them into the kingdom of his Son.

verses.text: “Who rescued us from the authority of darkness, and transferred us to the kingdom of the Son of His love, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.”

events.title: The Christ Hymn: Image of the Invisible God
events.detail: One of the highest statements of Christ's identity in the New Testament: image of the invisible God, agent and goal of all creation, head of the church, the one in whom everything holds together and through whom everything is reconciled.

verses.text: “In Him all things were created… all things have been created through Him and for Him. And He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.”
“In Him all the fullness of God was pleased to dwell, and through Him to reconcile all things to Himself, having made peace through the blood of His cross.”

events.title: Reconciled: Paul's Ministry to Make Known the Mystery
events.detail: Once alienated enemies, the Colossians have been reconciled through Christ's death, and Paul describes his own suffering as filling up what remains of Christ's afflictions on behalf of the church, in service of a mystery now revealed: Christ in you.

verses.text: “The riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.”

eras.label: Era Two · Colossians 2
eras.name: Complete in Christ, Not in Empty Philosophy
eras.dates: A direct confrontation with a local mix of philosophy, legalism, and angel-worship threatening to steal the church's confidence

events.title: Paul's Struggle for a Church He's Never Met
events.detail: Paul names his intense concern for Colossae and neighboring Laodicea, people he has never met face to face, hoping their hearts will be knit together in love and full assurance of understanding.

verses.text: “The full knowledge of God's mystery, that is, Christ Himself, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.”

events.title: Warning Against Hollow Philosophy: The Fullness of Deity
events.detail: Paul names the threat directly: a philosophy built on human tradition and 'elementary principles' rather than Christ: answered with the flat claim that the fullness of Deity dwells in Christ bodily, and believers are filled in him.

verses.text: “See to it that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deception, according to the tradition of men, according to the elementary principles of the world, and not according to Christ.”
“In Him all the fullness of Deity dwells bodily, and in Him you have been filled, who is the head over all rule and authority.”

events.title: Circumcision of Christ, Buried and Raised in Baptism
events.detail: Baptism is pictured as a circumcision made without hands: a burial and resurrection with Christ that cancels a legal record of debt and puts every hostile ruler and authority on public, defeated display.

verses.text: “Having canceled out the certificate of debt… having nailed it to the cross. Having disarmed the rulers and authorities, He made a public display of them, having triumphed over them.”

events.title: Don't Let Anyone Judge You: Food, Festivals, Angels, Asceticism
events.detail: Paul names the specific pressures the Colossians faced: dietary rules, festival observance, angel worship, and severe body-denying asceticism, all dismissed as a shadow next to the substance, which is Christ.

verses.text: “Things which are only a shadow of what is to come; but the substance belongs to Christ.”

eras.label: Era Three · Colossians 3
eras.name: Put On the New Self
eras.dates: Death, resurrection, and a wardrobe change, stripping off the old self's vices and clothing the new self in love

events.title: Seek the Things Above
events.detail: Since they've been raised with Christ, Paul tells the Colossians to set their minds on heaven, not earth: their real life is already hidden with Christ in God, waiting to be revealed when he appears.

verses.text: “For you died and your life has been hidden with Christ in God.”

events.title: Put Off the Old Self
events.detail: A vice list to be put to death (sexual immorality, anger, slander, lying) tied to putting off an old identity entirely, replaced by a new humanity where ethnic and social categories no longer define anyone.

verses.text: “A renewal in which there is no distinction between Greek and Jew, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, and freeman, but Christ is all and in all.”

events.title: Put On the New Self: Let the Peace of Christ Rule
events.detail: The positive counterpart to the vice list: compassion, kindness, humility, patience, and above everything love: the bond that holds the new self together, with Christ's peace ruling as umpire in the heart.

verses.text: “Above all these things put on love, which is the perfect bond of unity. And let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts.”

events.title: Household Code: Wives, Husbands, Children, Slaves
events.detail: A household code addressed pair by pair: wives and husbands, children and fathers, and at greatest length, slaves, told to work heartily as for the Lord and not merely for human masters.

verses.text: “Whatever you do, do your work heartily, as for the Lord rather than for men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance.”

eras.label: Era Four · Colossians 4
eras.name: Wise Speech and Final Greetings
eras.dates: The household code's final pair, then prayer, careful speech toward outsiders, and a long list of names closing the letter

events.title: Masters, Be Just to Your Slaves
events.detail: The household code's closing half-pair: masters are told to give their slaves what is right and fair, on the reminder that they too answer to a Master in heaven.

verses.text: “Masters, show to your slaves what is right and fair, knowing that you too have a Master in heaven.”

events.title: Prayer and Wise Speech Toward Outsiders
events.detail: Paul asks for prayer that a door would open for his imprisoned preaching, then turns to the Colossians' own conduct toward non-believers: wise, time-redeeming, and gracious, 'seasoned with salt.'

verses.text: “Let your words always be with grace, seasoned with salt, so that you will know how you should answer each person.”

events.title: Final Greetings: Tychicus, Onesimus, and ‘Remember My Chains’
events.detail: A long list of co-workers closes the letter, including Onesimus (the runaway slave of Philemon, here called 'faithful and beloved,' now traveling back to Colossae alongside Tychicus) and Paul's own handwritten sign-off.

verses.text: “With him Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you.” — the same Onesimus at the center of Paul's letter to Philemon, likely carried alongside this one.
“The greeting is in my own hand—Paul. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.”
